title: Plumbing & electrical rough-in
headline: Pipes and conduits go into walls and floors before plastering hides them for good.
seoTitle: Plumbing and electrical rough-in for Nigerian homes: what to check before plastering
seoDescription: How pipes, drainage, conduits and wiring are installed before plaster, common shortcuts, what to ask and the photos you need from your contractor.
summary: Once plaster goes on, you can’t see what is behind it. Get photos of every wall before it is covered.
duration: 1–3 weeks for rough-in, with final fixing after finishes [CHECK]
whatHappens: Electrical: conduit pipes chased into walls and laid in slabs, boxes for sockets and switches, route to the distribution board (DB), and earthing (earth rod/pit).
Wiring pulled through conduits with the right cable sizes for lighting, sockets and heavy loads such as AC units and cookers. [CHECK cable sizes with your electrician]
Plumbing: cold and hot water pipes (PPR or PVC), connections for each fitting, and pressure testing before closing up.
Drainage: waste and soil pipes with correct falls to inspection chambers, septic tank and soak-away (or public sewer where available).
Provision for water storage (overhead tank stand), borehole connection and pump.
problems: Undersized cables or no earthing — a fire and shock risk.
Conduits left out and cables buried directly in plaster.
Pipes not pressure-tested, leaking later behind tiles.
Drainage with poor falls that blocks; septic tank too small or too close to a borehole. [CHECK required separation distances]
Cheap fittings substituted for the specified brands.
questions: What cable sizes are used for lights, sockets and AC/cooker circuits?
Where is the earth rod and how is it connected?
What pipe type and brand, and has the system been pressure-tested? Can I see the test?
What size is the septic tank and how far is it from the borehole and the building?
Who will certify the electrical installation before connection? [CHECK local DisCo requirements]
